history.text: Portuguese sailors named the Wouri estuary Rio dos Camaroes, giving the country its name.
The territory was split into French and British mandates after the First World War.
French Cameroun became independent on 1 January.
British Southern Cameroons joined, forming a federal state.
A referendum replaced the federation with a unitary republic.

worthSeeing.title: Mount Cameroon:
worthSeeing.text: An active volcano and West Africa's highest peak, rising straight from the coast.

worthSeeing.title: Waza National Park:
worthSeeing.text: Savannah reserve in the far north known for elephants and birdlife.

worthSeeing.title: Foumban:
worthSeeing.text: The Bamoun royal palace and museum, centre of a long-standing sultanate.
